key_insight: Deep sequence models are more robust than strong tabular baselines for PV power forecasting when NWP inputs are noisy, and they adapt by shifting attention toward stable history and physical priors.
engineering_relevance: For PV forecasting systems, robustness under forecast uncertainty should be treated as a first-class design criterion alongside accuracy and latency when selecting models for deployment.
method: Physically constrained simulation using virtual PV power to isolate input-error propagation
Dynamic NWP perturbations with clear-sky-dependent heteroscedastic noise and Erbs-consistent radiation reconstruction
Compare six models with SHAP/Integrated Gradients plus Pareto analysis of accuracy, robustness, and latency
evidence_signal: The evaluation uses six representative models and tests them under temporally correlated, state-dependent NWP perturbations rather than idealized perfect-forecast conditions.
watch_item: Robustness conclusions come from a simulated virtual-PV framework, so real-plant effects and site-specific dynamics may still change model behavior in deployment.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
